title: Constant-line tensor and scalar Weil twist in the two coefficient models
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Write $J_X$ for the coefficient equivalence, with its induced equivalence on geometric-Frobenius Weil pairs, of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], from the common-stage model [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] to the PBC model [def-wf-weil-category].

For $b\in\Qlb^\times$ choose a finite coefficient field $E$ containing $b$, and let $(E_X,\theta_E)$ be the canonical constant Weil sheaf of [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]. Form the explicit PBC Weil line
$$\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{b,X_0}:=J_X(E_X,b\theta_E),$$
where $E_X$ denotes its common-stage image and the Frobenius of its $J_X$-image uses the pullback comparison specified with $J_X$. Its underlying integral representative is the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ in degree zero, rationalized and then included at the common stage $E$. The line is independent, up to the canonical scalar-extension identifications, of the finite field $E$; it is lisse of rank one. This construction is available also on disconnected schemes and on the empty scheme.

For every constructible common-stage Weil sheaf $\mathcal F=(M,\theta)$ of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], put $\mathcal F_b=(M,b\theta)$. The PBC tensor product of [def-wf-tensor-product] lies in the image of the constructible heart and admits a natural isomorphism of Weil pairs
$$\eta_{\mathcal F,b}:J_X(\mathcal F)\otimes\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{b,X_0}\xrightarrow{\sim}J_X(\mathcal F_b).$$
The underlying isomorphism is the completed derived right-unit map on the common integral representatives. These isomorphisms commute with finite coefficient extension and its associators. Consequently, transporting this PBC tensor back by $J_X^{-1}$ gives a constructible common-stage Weil sheaf isomorphic to $(M,b\theta)$. At every finite-extension rational point, and at each chosen geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ over a closed point, the induced linear stalk isomorphism intertwines the local geometric-Frobenius operators of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]; local operators on the transported tensor are thus conjugate to those on $\mathcal F_b$.

If $X_0$ is geometrically connected, choose a geometric point $\bar x\to X$ and the degree-one lift $s$ used in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. Then $X$ is connected, so the current [def-wf-fundamental-representation] construction applies, while [def-wf-weil-group] supplies $W(X_0)$ and its degree map. The line $\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{b,X_0}$ has trivial geometric monodromy and Weil representation $g\mapsto b^{\deg(g)}$. On this domain it is isomorphic to the line $\mathcal B_b$ of [def-wf-constant-weil-twist], and $\eta_{\mathcal F,b}$ identifies the tensor by that specified $\mathcal B_b$ with $J_X(\mathcal F_b)$.

source.place: First sentence: coefficient-model and constant-line identification implicit in the asserted local Frobenius rescaling

proof.text: Use the finite-stage equivalences $J_{X,E}$ and their common-stage equivalence in [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], including its final assertion for this separated finite-type $X_0$. These are identities on the common full integral category and on localized arrows. In particular their restriction to degree-zero objects uses the same constructible heart. Any given common-stage pair $(M,\theta)$ can be represented over one finite extension: represent $M,\theta,\theta^{-1}$ over finite stages and enlarge until the two inverse identities hold. This is exactly the common-stage equality convention of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-wf-weil-category]. Enlarge again to contain $b$, using [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. All subsequent constructions may therefore be checked at one such $E$, with no assumption that $\theta$ preserves an integral lattice. The scheme $X$ is separated of finite type over $k$ by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. Also $\ell$ is invertible on $X$ because $\ell\ne p$. These verify the hypotheses for the lisse comparisons below.

source.place: First sentence: passage between the two Weil coefficient models

proof.text: Put $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$. By [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible], $R[0]$ is derived complete, its reductions are the constant $(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_X[0]$, and its rationalization is the constant heart object $E_X$. The identity integral comparison in [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] gives precisely this same representative in PBC. Equip it with the specified $\theta_E$ of [def-weil-constant-weil-structure] and then multiply that isomorphism by $b$ after rationalization. Since $b\ne0$, its inverse is $b^{-1}\theta_E^{-1}$. This constructs the stated $\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{b,X_0}$. Its constant free rank-one reduction system is the unit of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. By [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison], its inverse-limit realization is the lisse completed module $R$; this is a comparison between the etale systems and pro-etale modules. By [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization], rational realization identifies the lisse heart coefficient unit with $R[1/\varpi_E]$ and respects pullback and finite coefficient extension. Together with the identity-on-integral-objects comparison $J$, this proves the lisse rank-one assertion in the stated coefficient model. This assertion is local on $X$ and uses no connectedness or base point. On the empty scheme it means locally free of rank one, a vacuous condition.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), Definition 6.8.3; constant Weil structure specified in the cited DAG definition

proof.text: For $E\subset L$ containing $b$, use the explicit canonical constant-object isomorphism $\alpha_{E,L}$ of [lem-weil-constant-weil-structure-stage-independence]. Its Weil equation for $\theta_E,\theta_L$ remains true for $b\theta_E,b\theta_L$: both sides of that equation are multiplied by the same scalar $b$. Apply the $E$-linear coefficient comparison and its maps $j_{X,L/E}$ of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison]. This gives the required identification of the PBC lines at the two stages. For three stages the constant-object identification is multiplication of coefficients: $(a\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto a\otimes st$. Thus the two composites agree under the specified balancing associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]; the maps $j$ satisfy the same cocycle by the comparison lemma. Two unrelated choices of $E$ are compared over their finite compositum [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set].

source.place: First sentence: independence of the constant line from its finite coefficient stage

proof.text:
For an integral representative $K$ of $M$, let $C$ denote the Koszul completion functor and $u_K:K\to C(K)$ its natural unit. The ordinary derived right unitor $r_K:K\otimes_R^L R\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ is supplied by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. On a K-flat representative it is the chain map $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$, with inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Define
$$\widehat r_K=u_K^{-1}\circ C(r_K):C(K\otimes_R^LR)\longrightarrow K.$$
The unit $u_K$ is invertible because $K$ is complete [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector]. Both factors are isomorphisms. This is exactly the completed tensor with the constant coefficient object in [def-wf-tensor-product]. The naturality of $r$ and $u$ makes $\widehat r$ natural in $K$; rationalization gives it on localized morphisms as well. Explicitly multiplication on either tensor factor by a scalar multiplies $\widehat r$ by that scalar, by the displayed chain formula and the localized-morphism rule in the tensor definition.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.9; Stacks Tags 0FPT, 099B and 0A0E

proof.text:
Write $P$ for PBC Frobenius pullback, $\varphi$ for the image of $\theta$ under the specified pullback comparison of $J$, and $e:P(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ for the coefficient isomorphism. Here $e$ is the image of $\theta_E$: both use the maps fixing each constant section at every quotient level [def-weil-constant-weil-structure, def-wf-tensor-product, lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison]. Before completion the strong monoidal pullback law for right unitors in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] says
$$r_{PK}\circ(1\otimes e)\circ t=P(r_K).$$
It also holds for the completed maps: the completion comparison in [def-wf-tensor-product] carries $u_N$ to $u_{PN}$, since on the $m$-th Koszul component it fixes the degree-zero inclusion and its shifted-product component is zero. Naturality of $u$ and inversion of $u_K,u_{PK}$ therefore give the same equation for $\widehat r$ and $\mu$. Combining with naturality for $\varphi$, and then using scalar bilinearity from step 4, gives
$$\widehat r_K\circ(\varphi\otimes b e)\circ\mu=(b\varphi)\circ P(\widehat r_K).$$
This is the Weil-morphism equation. Its inverse is a Weil morphism by multiplying this equation by the inverse maps. Thus $\widehat r_K$ gives the required $\eta_{\mathcal F,b}$ at $E$.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; right-unit normalization of the specified pullback comparison

proof.text: Check coefficient compatibility on the integral representatives, before allowing $b$ or $\theta$ to have denominators. For $E\subset L$ write $S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,X}$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $S$ is finite free over $R$, $K\otimes_R^LS$ is complete, and the specified map $\chi_{L/E,K}$ identifies ordinary extension with the strict-tower extension. Ordinary scalar extension is the ringed-topos pullback for the identity site and $R\to S$. Its right-unitor square commutes by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]: both chain maps take $(x\otimes a)\otimes s$ to $x\otimes as$. This also proves the square for completed unitors. Indeed $K\otimes_R^LR\cong K$ and its scalar extension are complete, so the completion units are invertible; naturality of those units in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] reduces the completed square to that ordinary square. Naturality of $\chi$ applies both to $r_K$ and to these invertible completion units; conjugating by $\chi$ therefore gives the same square for the specified strict-tower extension. Rationalize and use the maps $j$ and the pullback compatibility in [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison]. The resulting square is exactly coefficient extension of $\eta_{\mathcal F,b}$ versus $\eta_{\mathcal F_L,b}$, with the line identification of step 3.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and completion construction in 3.4.9-3.4.12; Stacks Tag 07A4 for scalar pullback

proof.text: For $E\subset L\subset H$, apply step 6 successively. Under the specified scalar associator, both iterated right-unit maps send $((x\otimes a)\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $x\otimes(ast)$. This is the balancing associator of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]; its unit and pentagon equations and the unit/cocycle equations for $j$ in [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] make the identifications independent of further extension. Consequently the finite-stage $\eta$ descend to a natural common-stage isomorphism. Its source is in the image of the constructible heart because its target is $J_X(M,b\theta)$ and its underlying map is an isomorphism. Applying the inverse equivalence gives a constructible common-stage Weil sheaf isomorphic to $(M,b\theta)$. Naturality follows from that of $\widehat r$: for a commuting pair-map $f$, $f\widehat r_M=\widehat r_N(f\otimes1)$, first at a common finite stage and then in the Hom colimit.

source.place: First sentence: tensor by the constant Weil line interpreted in the common-stage model

proof.text:
Let $u$ be the resulting common-stage isomorphism from the transported tensor to $\mathcal F_b$. For any Weil-pair isomorphism $u:(A,\psi_A)\to(B,\psi_B)$, induction on $n$ in its commuting square gives
$$u\psi_A^{[n]}=\psi_B^{[n]}P^n(u).$$
Pull this identity back to a point occurring in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Naturality of the point-transport maps, including at $\Qlb$, is precisely [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural]. Together with naturality of the composition comparisons in the definition, it moves the stalk map through every factor of the local-operator composite. Hence $u_{\bar x}F_A^{(n)}=F_B^{(n)}u_{\bar x}$, and the same formula holds at a closed point with $n$ its degree. The stalk map is an isomorphism since it is the image of $u$ under a functor; on degree-zero cohomology it is the asserted linear conjugacy. No local operator at an arbitrary generic geometric point is asserted.

source.place: First sentence: compatibility of the tensor identification with local geometric Frobenius

proof.text: Use the scheme hypotheses verified in step 1. The reduction/inverse-limit equivalence and rational full faithfulness of [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison], followed by the unit, pullback and fibre comparisons of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization], identify our coefficient line and its Frobenius with the constant lisse system and its rationalized map. Thus the classical lisse representation construction applies to this line, with the same fibre maps. Assume $X_0$ geometrically connected and make the choices in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. The constant lisse line has trivial geometric monodromy by the unit assertion of [cor-galois-lisse-representations]. Every natural fibre path fixes each element of a constant finite reduction sheaf: an element is a map from the terminal finite cover to the constant finite cover, and naturality fixes its image. Passing through inverse limits and rationalization shows that the specified $L_s$ on this line is identity in the constant basis. The canonical $\theta_E$ fixes the same basis [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]. Therefore the formula $T_s=\varphi_{\bar x}L_s^{-1}$ gives $T_s=b$ for $b\theta_E$. Every $g=hs^n$ has $\deg(g)=n$ by [def-wf-weil-group], and the extension formula in [def-wf-fundamental-representation] gives $\rho(g)=1\cdot b^n$. This includes negative $n$ since $b$ is invertible; the character is continuous because the degree map has discrete target.

source.place: First sentence: identification of the constant Weil line with the character b to the degree

proof.text: The line $\mathcal B_b$ specified in [def-wf-constant-weil-twist], on this connected domain, has the same trivial geometric representation and degree-one operator $b$. Choose the linear isomorphism of its one-dimensional fibre with that of $\widetilde{\mathcal B}_{b,X_0}$. The fully faithful lisse equivalence of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2) gives a unique underlying lisse-sheaf isomorphism with that fibre map. Transfer this map through the fully faithful rational realization of [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] and the fully faithful lisse-heart realization of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization], using $J$ as in step 2. Their pullback comparisons identify the classical Weil square with the framework square. It commutes with Frobenius: after taking the fibre, the Weil square is the equality with the two operators $T_s=b$, using naturality of the specified path $L_s$ in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]; faithfulness then gives the sheaf square. Thus it is an isomorphism of Weil lines. Tensor this isomorphism with $J_X(\mathcal F)$ and follow with $\eta_{\mathcal F,b}$ from step 7. This proves the last clause for the specified $\mathcal B_b$, and concludes all assertions.
